rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: this position comes from a Semi-Slav game played on Lichess. Black is a knight up for a pawn.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.e2: Two pieces on the same line, the more valuable one in front: once attacked, the front one moves and gives up the one behind. This is the skewer, the pin reversed.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.p: The black queen on c6 and the rook on e8 stand on the same diagonal. Find the best move.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.certo: The bishop goes to b5, defended by the rook on b3, and attacks the queen. Behind it, on the same diagonal, stands the rook on e8.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is to bring the bishop to b5: it attacks the queen, and the rook on e8 stands behind it on the same diagonal.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d3e4.1: The bishop captures the knight on e4.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d3e4.2: With this move Black has a resource: the pawn recaptures on e4, and Black stays a piece up.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d3e4.3: Back to the position: look for the attack on the queen that leaves the piece behind exposed.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d1h5.1: The queen goes to h5 and attacks the rook on e8.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d1h5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the bishop goes to a6, and the rook on a8 now defends the one on e8. Black stays a piece up.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d1h5.3: Back to the position: attack the front piece, the queen on c6.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d1c2.1: The queen goes to c2 and defends the bishop on d3.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.err.d1c2.2: With this move Black has a resource: the bishop goes to a6 and attacks your bishop on d3. Black stays a piece up.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not attack the queen on c6. Look for the attack that leaves the piece behind exposed.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: attack the queen on c6.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.l0: The queen on c6 is attacked, and capturing the bishop costs the queen. It must leave the diagonal.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.l1: Black moves the queen to c7 so as not to lose it. The rook on e8 is left exposed on the bishop's diagonal.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.l2: The bishop captures the rook on e8. White was a piece down and now has the material advantage.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex1.l3: In positions like this, with two pieces on the same line and the more valuable one in front, attack the front one: it moves, and the one behind falls.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.err.salto: Back to the position: the white queen is pinned. Look for the attack on it that leaves the piece behind exposed.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now with Black, in a game played on Lichess. Your queen on c6 pins the white queen on e4 to the king on h1.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.e2: A piece pinned to the king cannot leave the line. If it is the front piece of a skewer, it cannot even capture its attacker.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.p: The white queen is pinned, and behind it, on the e-file, stands the rook on e1. Find the best move.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.certo: The rook goes to e8 and attacks the queen. Pinned, the queen can neither capture the rook nor leave the diagonal.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is to bring the rook to e8: the pinned queen cannot capture it, and the rook on e1 stands behind it.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.err.c6e4.1: Your queen captures the queen on e4.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.err.c6e4.2: With this move White has a resource: the rook on f4 recaptures and attacks the knight. White keeps a rook against a knight.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.err.d4c2.1: The knight goes to c2 and attacks the rook on e1.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.err.d4c2.2: With this move White has a resource: the queen captures your queen on c6, and the pin is gone. The rook on e1 escapes afterwards.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not attack the pinned queen. Look for the attack that leaves the piece behind exposed.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: attack the pinned queen along the e-file.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.l0: The queen on e4 is attacked and can only move along the diagonal of the pin. White's best way out is to capture your queen.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.l1: The white queen captures your queen on c6. By leaving e4, it opens the e-file to the rook on e1.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook captures the rook on e1 with check.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.l3: The king steps out of check to g2.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.l4: The knight recaptures the queen on c6 and escapes the rook on f4. Black is a knight up.
rot.skewer.ideia.ex2.l5: In positions like this, a piece pinned to the king cannot answer the skewer: attack it, and the piece behind falls.
rot.skewer.demos.rei.1: Attack: this position comes from a game played on Lichess. The black king on f8 and the rook on c8 stand on the eighth rank.
rot.skewer.demos.rei.2: The rook gives check on h8. The king is the front piece: in check, it is forced to leave the rank.
rot.skewer.demos.rei.3: The king steps to e7, because nothing can block on g8. Any king move leaves the rook on c8 exposed.
rot.skewer.demos.rei.4: The rook captures the rook on c8. With the king in front, the skewer is at its strongest: the king cannot stay on the line.
rot.skewer.demos.reiPretas.1: Attack: now with Black, in another game played on Lichess. The white king on e1 and the rook on h1 stand on the first rank.
rot.skewer.demos.reiPretas.2: The rook gives check on c1. The king is in front, and the rook on h1 behind it, on the same rank.
rot.skewer.demos.reiPretas.3: In check, the king cannot castle; it steps to e2, because no white piece can block on d1. The rook on h1 is left exposed.
rot.skewer.demos.reiPretas.4: The rook captures the rook on h1. Black wins a rook.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.1: Attack: White again, in a game played on Lichess. Black threatens mate: the rook on b1 wants to go to h1.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.2: The bishop gives check on f7. It looks like a skewer, but behind the king, on the diagonal to a2, there is no black piece.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.3: The king steps to c5, and nothing falls behind it. The mate threat on h1 remains, and White is lost.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: before the check, see what stands behind the king. On the other diagonal stands the bishop on f3.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.5: The bishop gives check on c6, and behind the king stands the bishop on f3, the piece that helps with the mate.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.6: The king steps to c4, and the bishop on f3 is left exposed.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.7: The bishop captures on f3 and now watches h1: the mate is gone, and White is a piece up.
rot.skewer.demos.excecao.8: In positions like this, not every check along a line is a skewer: see what stands behind the king. The position decides.
rot.skewer.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Now with White. Your rook can capture the bishop on e5 with check. Is the capture worth it? Find the best move.
rot.skewer.pratica.valeAqui.fim: On f3 the rook gave check, with the rook on f7 behind the king. The king went to e4, and the rook captured the one on f7.
rot.skewer.pratica.valeAqui.err.e3e5: The rook captures the bishop with check, but the king recaptures: you give the rook for a bishop. See what stands behind the king, on the f-file.
rot.skewer.pratica.valeAqui.err.f8h7: The knight captures the pawn on h7, but the bishop goes to d4 and pins your rook to the king. See what stands behind the black king.
rot.skewer.pratica.valeAqui.err.g3g4: The pawn gives check, but the king goes to f4, attacks your rook, and nothing falls behind it. Look for a check on the f-file.
rot.skewer.pratica.damaFrente.enunciado: Now with White, in a Sicilian game. Look at the open lines. Find the best move.
rot.skewer.pratica.damaFrente.fim: On f3 the bishop attacked the queen, and behind it stood the rook on a8. The queen went to d6, and the bishop captured the rook.
rot.skewer.pratica.damaFrente.err.calmo: The rook gets active, but the black queen stays comfortable on d5. See what stands behind the black queen.
rot.skewer.pratica.comCravada.enunciado: Now with Black. See which white piece is pinned. Find the best move.
rot.skewer.pratica.comCravada.fim: On e6 the rook captured the rook, and the pinned queen could not recapture. It captured your queen, and the rook captured on e1 with check.
rot.skewer.pratica.comCravada.err.c5e3: The queen captures the queen with check, but the rook on e6 recaptures, and the pin is gone. Use the pinned queen: it cannot capture on e6.
rot.skewer.pratica.comCravada.err.d5d4: The pawn attacks the queen, but it closes your queen's diagonal: the pin is gone, and the rook on e6 gives check on e8. Use the pin while the diagonal is open.
rot.skewer.pratica.comCravada.err2.c8c5: The rook recaptures the queen, but the rook on e1 captures your rook on e6. First capture the rook on e1, with check.
